dismissals: Rename, duplicate, create, and archive mutate brand data; menu labels fully describe them, and Archive is destructive.
All mutate template/brand data; Delete is destructive. Menu contents are fully mapped without operating them.
Both create or materially edit template assets; mapped but not operated to preserve state.
Creates a brand workflow; skipped to preserve state.
Changing paint type would alter the selected brand color; options are fully visible and mapped.
Externally visible member-invitation action; safety harness explicitly blocks operating it.
Virtualized draft-card titles, ellipsis buttons, and repeated card controls are content rows; one representative card menu has already been mapped.
Repeated virtualized draft-card content and per-card menus; representative card interaction was already explored, and opening documents could alter state.
macOS system menu items are OS-level, destructive/session-changing, or unrelated to Yarn app navigation.
macOS recent-app/document entries are system content, not Yarn surfaces; opening them would leave the app.
Standard macOS app menu commands are quit/hide/about/services rather than Yarn workspace functionality; several are destructive or leave app state.
Standard macOS text-editing commands are contextual and may mutate focused content; no new Yarn surface is expected.
Electron reload/devtools/zoom/full-screen commands are shell controls and may disrupt the exploration state.
Standard macOS window-management commands do not expose Yarn features and would alter the window layout.
OS window-layout commands are unrelated to app functionality and would change the window arrangement.

Agent model dropdown options were fully enumerated without changing the current selection.

Existing overlay-template preview would insert document content, so it was intentionally not selected.
Recent-media thumbnails would insert assets and upload would open a file flow; neither was operated to preserve the draft.
Menu actions were already inspected; remaining entries would copy/download/duplicate/delete or change brand, aspect ratio, or performance settings, so they are unsafe or state-mutating to operate.
These are disabled generic macOS text-substitution menu items, not Yarn app controls.

Disabled generic macOS window tiling commands, unrelated to Yarn functionality.

This media card and its options are repetitive library content; selecting it would insert content into the document.

This is another repetitive media-grid options control; individual asset selection would mutate the draft.

This is a macOS system-settings action outside Yarn; opening it would leave the target app and is irrelevant to the Yarn navigation map.

This is an existing template/content row; selecting it is unnecessary because the Templates surface, details pane, and options menu are already mapped.

These are non-navigational media-status labels or already-observed numeric/value controls inside mapped editor, caption, settings, and media surfaces; operating them would either mutate document/workspace state or add no navigation knowledge.

These are already-mapped caption/color/sort/info values and individual font choices from the brand typography picker. Selecting them would change document or brand state; the font picker and current selections are already documented.
These are individual font-family choices in the already-mapped brand typography picker. Choosing any would mutate the brand font default; they are repetitive content rather than new navigation.
These are individual font-family choices or a generic typography-list label in the already-mapped brand font picker. Choosing a font would mutate brand state; none opens a distinct surface.

Add scene and Add Size would mutate document/workspace state; Agent is an already-mapped editor tab; Alejandro and Alice are voice choices whose selection would mutate the current project. None needs operation to expose new navigation.
Voice/cursor selections would mutate the current project or defaults; AutoTime is a content timestamp. These settings and voice picker categories are already mapped and need no further operation.
These are individual caption font-family options; selecting any would mutate document caption styling, while the picker behavior is already mapped.
These are individual caption font-family options; selecting any would change document styling, and the font picker interaction is already documented.

Font-family rows would change document caption styling; Brynn would change the document voice; By Page would change caption grouping. Brand Kit navigation was already fully explored earlier, so reopening it adds no coverage.

These are caption font-family options or voice choices from already-mapped document pickers. Selecting one would change the draft; duplicate Cereal instances are covered by the same non-mutating rationale.

This mixed batch is already-covered or unsafe: font/voice choices and caption padding would mutate the draft; the project row is content; Copy actions would alter clipboard/project state; Notion integration would affect an external account; Custom 1 window size was already inspected.

These controls were already mapped or would mutate state: fonts/voice/theme/speed/performance choices, workspace selection, destructive deletes, duplication, and profile-photo editing. Duplicate label instances are covered together.

Font and voice options would mutate document styling/voice; Effort buttons would change the document-local agent override. The English category tab and effort behavior were already explored, so no additional surface remains.

Font/voice/music/sound/animation choices would change the draft or defaults; Export is externally consequential. Everything and Eyedropper were already inspected as picker controls, and Fixed is an already-covered option/state.

Font-family choices in caption styling; selecting one would mutate the document, and the font-picker behavior is already mapped.
Individual voice choices in the document voice picker; selecting one would mutate the project voice, and voice categories/options are already mapped.
Native macOS window-zoom control; operating it changes window geometry and adds no Yarn-specific navigation knowledge.

Grid is a nonessential view-mode toggle; High and Hug Lines are already-observed current document styling/runtime choices whose selection could alter or reapply document state. Their parent controls and option sets are already mapped.
Hide is a current cursor/visibility choice already mapped; Import begins a file-import flow that could change document/workspace content, so neither needs operation for navigation mapping.
Individual voice choices in the document voice picker; selecting them changes project voice. The picker categories and complete option pattern are already mapped.
Light is an individual font-weight choice and Low is an agent-effort option; selecting either would alter document/runtime state. Both parent controls and option sets are already mapped.
List is a redundant display-mode toggle already mapped; Make a copy creates persistent duplicate content and is intentionally not operated under safety rules.
Medium is an individual caption weight/effort choice and the other two are voice choices; selecting these would change document/runtime state, while their parent pickers are fully mapped.
These controls create, move, or insert persistent workspace/document content; intentionally not operated under non-mutating exploration rules.
Newest first is the already-observed current sort option, and No background track is a document music choice; selecting them is unnecessary and the containing controls are already mapped.
This generic informational affordance was observed on Brand Colors guidance; its setting context is already recorded, and opening another help tooltip adds no navigation path.

These are leaf choices in already-mapped dropdowns/toggles (font/default, settings toggles, sort, caption preset); selecting them could alter state or merely reapply a current option, so no further surface would be discovered.
Publish is externally visible; Remove controls are destructive; Rename edits persistent project/brand content. These actions are intentionally not operated.
Individual voice options; selection changes the document voice and the voice picker has already been mapped.
Existing project row in Add from Library; selecting it would insert/reuse content in the current document, and the Projects tab structure is already mapped.
The editor Script tab was already visited and mapped; re-operating it would not discover a new surface.
Search fields on already-mapped list/picker surfaces; entering text only filters repetitive content and reveals no new navigation surface.
Individual voice option; selection changes document voice and the picker is already mapped.
Leaf choices in already-mapped settings/sort controls; selecting could change brand/document defaults or reapply display state, with no new surface to discover.
Account/integration authentication actions are externally consequential and intentionally not operated.
Already-mapped sort, paint-picker format, theme choice, and editable template field. Operating them would only change or reapply state and would not reveal a new surface.
Individual voice choices; selection changes document voice and the voice picker is already mapped.

Existing template/project rows or editable content titles; opening/inserting/renaming them would enter or mutate persistent content. Their surrounding lists and interaction patterns are already mapped.
Repetitive existing project rows in the library/project picker; opening or selecting them would enter/insert content, while the list interaction pattern is already mapped.
Repetitive existing project rows; opening or selecting them would enter/insert content. The library and project-picker interaction patterns are already mapped.
Existing project rows; selecting them would enter or insert persistent content, and the project-list behavior is already mapped.
Upgrade is an account/billing action; Upload Camera Footage starts an external file/camera flow and would add content. Both are intentionally not operated.

Vintage Groove is a document music selection, Wizard a voice selection, and Z - A a leaf sort option. Their parent controls are mapped; selecting would change document/view state without revealing new surfaces.

The two remaining unnamed controls are unlabeled thumbnail/upload-strip internals from already-mapped media pickers; activating them could insert or upload content, so they are intentionally not operated.
